summary.purpose: Evaluate and update policy status lifecycle for TFG Personal Lines Policy Processing by reading validated policy master records, applying date-based status transition rules, and producing status-updated policy extracts with error reporting for date validation failures.
summary.high_level_narrative: The program initiates by retrieving the system current date and validating it as a legitimate calendar date. It then opens three sequential files: POLICY-IN for input policy records, POLICY-OUT for updated policy output, and ERROR-OUT for date validation exceptions. The main processing loop reads each policy record from POLICY-IN, validates the effective date and expiry date as valid calendar dates, and ensures expiry date is not before effective date. If any validation fails, an error record with specific error code (S001, S002, S003) is written to ERROR-OUT. For valid records, the program determines the new policy status: preserves 'CN' (Cancelled) if already cancelled; otherwise assigns 'PN' (Pending) if current date is before effective date, 'AC' (Active) if current date falls on or between effective and expiry dates, or 'EX' (Expired) if current date exceeds expiry date. When the status changes, the PO-UPDATE-DT field is set to the current system date. The updated policy record is written to POLICY-OUT. Counters track reads, writes, status changes, and each status category. Upon end-of-file, all files are closed and processing statistics are displayed.

knowledge_profile.purpose: Evaluate and Update Policy Status Lifecycle for TFG Personal Lines Policy Processing. Reads validated policy master records, validates effective and expiry dates, determines current policy status based on business rules, and writes status-updated policy extract and date validation exceptions.
key_logic: Initialize system current date and validate it as a calendar date.
Open input file POLICY-IN and output files POLICY-OUT and ERROR-OUT; handle open errors.
Read each policy record from POLICY-IN sequentially until end of file or fatal error.
For each record: validate effective date (calendar date), validate expiry date (calendar date), ensure expiry date is not before effective date.
If any validation fails, write error record to ERROR-OUT with appropriate error code (S001, S002, S003) and increment rejected counter.

If validations pass, determine new policy status: preserve 'CN' if existing status is 'CN'; else if current date < effective date set 'PN' (Pending); else if current date <= expiry date set 'AC' (Active); else set 'EX' (Expired).
If status changed, update PO-UPDATE-DT to current date and increment changed counter.
Write updated policy record to POLICY-OUT.
Increment counters for each status category (Pending, Active, Expired, Cancelled).
Close all files, display processing statistics, set return code if fatal errors occurred.

business_rules: If existing policy status is 'CN' (Cancelled), preserve 'CN' regardless of dates.
If current system date is before policy effective date, status becomes 'PN' (Pending).
If current system date is on or after effective date but on or before expiry date, status becomes 'AC' (Active).
If current system date is after expiry date, status becomes 'EX' (Expired).
Effective date must be a valid calendar date (YYYYMMDD).
Expiry date must be a valid calendar date (YYYYMMDD).
Expiry date must not be earlier than effective date.
Policy records failing any date validation are written to ERROR-OUT with specific error codes (S001, S002, S003) and not written to POLICY-OUT.
Only records passing all validations are written to POLICY-OUT with updated status.
If policy status changes, the update date (PO-UPDATE-DT) is set to current system date.
